mateo: Quick q — SAST flagged `hardcoded_key_usage` in `api/crypto/wrappers.go` but it's just a thin wrapper that calls our KMS. Seems like a false positive. Anyone know what evidence the scanner team wants to close these?

olivia: can you paste the snippet or a link to the file/PR?

mateo: sure — here's the call site (redacted):
```go
// wrappers.go
func DecryptBlob(ctx context.Context, keyID string, blob []byte) ([]byte, error) {
    // keyID comes from env.KMS_KEY_ID, not a literal
    return kmsClient.Decrypt(ctx, &kms.DecryptInput{KeyId: aws.String(keyID), CiphertextBlob: blob})
}
```
scanner is flagging because it sees `KeyId` and a string-like var.

emily: this is a pretty common FP. The scanner regex heuristics catch the pattern. Usual evidence for exemption: (1) runtime audit log showing a Decrypt event tied to the service principal, (2) key policy snippet or IAM binding proving only runtime SA can use the key, (3) a short note explaining why the value isn't a hardcoded secret.

shiv: +1. @mateo can you grab a KMS audit event snippet from the last 24h showing the Decrypt call? the exemptions team looks for timestamps/arn/service-account.

mateo: pasted an anonymized event below:
`{ "eventName": "Decrypt", "principal": "serviceAccount:infra-runtime@redwood-prod", "resourceName": "projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/ck-1", "timestamp": "2024-04-09T18:12:03Z" }`

security-bot: Created exemption request SEC-3124 for SAST false positive reported by mateo. Link: https://sec-tracker.redwood/SEC-3124 :robot_face:

carlos: small RBAC note — the code-scanner service account doesn't have access to read KMS audit logs, so sometimes scanner team can't auto-verify evidence. We either allow read on the logging resource scoped to the service or have the runtime team attach evidence in the ticket. Avoid giving broad logs access.

sre-oncall: fyi we had a leak last year when logs.viewer was applied at org-level to a CI SA. prefer resource-scoped `roles/logging.viewer` on `projects/redwood-prod` or create a tiny accessor that only reads AuditLog entries.

olivia: for KMS, you can also show the key policy that restricts Decrypt to the runtime SA and maybe the infra admins. That plus audit log is sufficient for most reviewers. Scanner doesn't need to run with KMS read perms if teams attach evidence to SEC ticket.

mateo: opened PR with exemption + attached evidence: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4821 — includes anonymized audit JSON and key policy snippet.

emily: can you also add a comment in the scanning config to whitelist this pattern with a link to SEC-3124? helps future triage.

shiv: and we should update the playbook: add a new flow for "crypto wrapper FP" — steps: collect audit event, attach key policy, create SEC ticket, add temporary suppression, monitor 7 days after suppression, then permanently suppress if no regressions. Assign owner.

security-bot: SEC-3124 updated: assignee=olivia, status=triage, due=2024-05-10.

olivia: I'll review the PR today. @mateo please include the IAM snippet you used to restrict decrypt to the runtime SA (redact full ARNs).

mateo: added the IAM snippet and rotation doc (link) plus a small `evidence/` folder with redacted lines. PR updated.

carlos: post-merge action: ops should kick a re-scan and confirm the same finding is suppressed. then monitor logs for 7 days per playbook. If anything odd, re-open SEC-3124.

emily: I'll add the re-scan + monitoring to the next release checklist.

mateo: no blockers from my side. thanks all for the quick help. :tada:

olivia: thanks. I'll mark SEC-3124 as 'approved for suppression' after PR merges and monitoring window is set. :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: note for runbook: do not grant scanner SA broad logging roles. I'll draft a short snippet on safe scoping and share in #eng-sre.

mateo: ack. closing loop once merged.

security-bot: SEC-3124 comment added: "evidence attached by reporter; RBAC changes not required; suppression window set to 7 days"

olivia: closing — will follow up in SEC ticket if anything else crops up. :wave:
